parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A student observes different stars from the Earth.
Give two reasons why some stars appear brighter than others.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State what is meant by a standard candle.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: A spectral line from a star within a galaxy is observed to have a wavelength of 660.9 nm. The same spectral line measured in the laboratory is observed to have a wavelength of 656.3 nm.
parts.text: Show that the speed of the star relative to the Earth is 2.1 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the distance to the star.

The Hubble constant is 2.3 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: State and explain what can be concluded about the Universe based on this change in observed wavelength.
